questions.q: A tenant has only Entra ID Free licensing. A cloud-only user forgets their password and tries to use self-service password reset. What is the outcome?
options: It works, because password reset for cloud-only users is included in every edition of Entra ID, including Free and trial tenants
It isn't covered; Free allows only password change, and reset needs Microsoft 365 Business Standard or higher, or Entra ID P1 or P2
It works only if the user has registered the Microsoft Authenticator app
It works only if the user is a member of a security group that is in scope
questions.explanation: In Free, cloud-only users can change a known password, but self-service reset for forgotten passwords needs Microsoft 365 Business Standard or higher, or Entra ID P1 or P2. A license is required for any user you intend to benefit from SSPR.

questions.q: A company with hybrid users licenses them only with Microsoft 365 Business Standard and wants SSPR password changes written back to on-premises Active Directory. What is the result?
options: It is supported, because Microsoft 365 Business Standard includes password writeback through Entra Connect Sync
It is supported only with Cloud Sync and not with Entra Connect Sync
It is supported only for users in protected groups
It isn't supported; writeback requires Entra ID P1 or P2, or Microsoft 365 Business Premium
questions.explanation: Standalone Microsoft 365 Basic and Standard plans don't support SSPR with on-premises writeback. Writeback requires Entra ID P1, P2 or Microsoft 365 Business Premium.

questions.q: SSPR requires one authentication method, and many users have registered only one. The administrator changes the policy to require two methods. What happens to users who have only one registered method?
options: They can't reset or unlock their password until they register another method
They can still reset with their one method until the next scheduled reconfirmation of their authentication information
They are enrolled automatically in an email method and can reset immediately
They are locked out of all sign-ins until an administrator resets them
questions.explanation: If users have fewer methods registered than the policy requires, they see an error and must contact an administrator or register more. Increase the requirement only after users have registered enough methods.

questions.q: Before migrating to the centralized Authentication methods policy, an SSPR policy requires one method, and the only method enabled is Microsoft Authenticator. What is the guidance?
options: Authenticator alone is sufficient and recommended because it supports both push notifications and codes
Require two methods so Authenticator can be used alone
Select at least one additional method, because Authenticator can't be the only method when one method is required
Enable only Authenticator notifications and disable verification codes
questions.explanation: Microsoft advises that Authenticator can't be selected as the only method when one method is required, and with two required you need at least two additional methods alongside it.

questions.q: What range of days can you configure before users are asked to reconfirm their authentication information for SSPR?
options: 1 to 365 days, where 365 means users are never asked
0 to 730 days, where 0 means users are never asked
30 to 90 days only
0 to 180 days, where 0 means at every sign-in
questions.explanation: Reconfirmation accepts 0 to 730 days, and 0 disables prompts. The option is available only when users are required to register when signing in.

questions.q: SSPR registration is required at sign-in and a user closes the registration window. What happens?
options: The user's account is disabled until registration is complete, and an administrator must re-enable it
The user is exempted from registration for 14 days
The user is signed out of the current session immediately
The user is prompted again at each sign-in until registration is complete, and the current session isn't broken
questions.explanation: Users can dismiss the SSPR registration page, but they are prompted every time they sign in until they finish. The interruption doesn't break an existing sign-in.

questions.q: An organization wants administrators to be able to reset their own passwords by using security questions only. What should the administrator do?
options: Nothing can change this; administrator accounts always use a two-gate policy that prohibits security questions
Enable security questions in the Authentication methods policy and scope them to a group that contains the administrators
Configure a custom administrator reset policy
Assign the Authentication Policy Administrator role to each administrator
questions.explanation: Administrators are subject to a built-in two-gate reset policy that requires two pieces of authentication data and prohibits security questions. It can't be changed and doesn't depend on the Authentication methods policy.

questions.q: An organization turns on the option to notify all admins when other admins reset their passwords. Who receives the notification?
options: Only the administrator who performed the reset
All users in the tenant
Global Administrators
Authentication Administrators
questions.explanation: When enabled, Global Administrators are emailed at their primary email address when another administrator changes their password through SSPR.

questions.q: A guest signs in with a personal outlook.com Microsoft account and tries to use Microsoft Entra SSPR to reset the account password. What happens?
options: It works, because all B2B guests can use SSPR with the email they registered, including personal Microsoft accounts
It works only if the guest registers a phone number
It works only in tenants that have Entra ID P2
It isn't supported; personal Microsoft accounts can't use Entra SSPR
questions.explanation: Microsoft accounts granted guest access, such as Outlook.com or Hotmail accounts, can't use Entra SSPR because their passwords are managed by the Microsoft account service.

questions.q: Which is the least-privileged role in this list for enabling password writeback in the SSPR on-premises integration settings?
options: Authentication Administrator
Hybrid Identity Administrator
Groups Administrator
Security Reader
questions.explanation: Microsoft's writeback tutorial calls for at least the Hybrid Identity Administrator role to enable the setting in the Entra admin center.

questions.q: Password writeback is enabled, but users get errors when resetting on-premises passwords. The connector account lacks permissions. Which set is required?
options: Replicate Directory Changes, Replicate Directory Changes All and Replicating Directory Changes In Filtered Set
Create child objects on the domain root only
Reset password, Change password, Write lockoutTime, Write pwdLastSet, and Unexpire Password
Full control on the Domain Controllers OU
questions.explanation: The writeback account needs rights to reset and change passwords and to write lockoutTime and pwdLastSet, plus Unexpire Password on the domain root. The replication permissions are for password hash synchronization.

questions.q: Password writeback fails when users reset their password more than once in a day. Which on-premises setting should you change?
options: Set Minimum password age to 0
Set Password history count to 0
Set Maximum password age to 0
Set Account lockout threshold to 0
questions.explanation: Writeback is subject to on-premises policy. To let users change or reset more than once per day, minimum password age must be 0.

questions.q: An administrator who forgot their on-premises password uses SSPR with password writeback, but the reset fails. The account belongs to a protected group. Why?
options: Administrators can't use SSPR at all
Writeback requires the administrator to be a member of a Microsoft 365 group with an active license
Writeback works only for cloud-only administrators
The writeback service account can't change passwords for users in protected groups
questions.explanation: Accounts in protected groups are controlled by AdminSDHolder, so writeback can't reset them. Administrators can change the cloud password but can't use writeback to reset a forgotten on-premises one.

questions.q: Which network connectivity does password writeback require?
options: Inbound TCP 443 from the internet to the Entra Connect server and outbound port 80
Outbound connections over port 443, with no inbound firewall rules
Inbound TCP 389 and 636 from Azure
A site-to-site VPN with Azure
questions.explanation: Writeback uses an Azure Service Bus relay, and all communication is outbound over port 443. No inbound rules are needed.

questions.q: Domain A uses Entra Connect Sync and disconnected domain B uses Cloud Sync. Users in both domains need SSPR writeback. What should you do?
options: Enable writeback in each tool and select both writeback options in the SSPR on-premises integration settings
Migrate domain B to Entra Connect Sync, because writeback works only with that tool and requires domain connectivity
Use Cloud Sync for both domains, because the tools can't run side by side
Select only the Cloud Sync writeback option, which covers both tools
questions.explanation: Password writeback works with Connect Sync and Cloud Sync, and they can be deployed side by side for different domains. In SSPR you can select both writeback checkboxes.

questions.q: Users must be able to unlock their on-premises account without resetting their password. Which SSPR setting enables this?
options: Notify users on password resets
Number of days before users must reconfirm their authentication information at sign-in
Allow users to unlock accounts without resetting their password
Require users to register when signing in
questions.explanation: By default, a reset also unlocks the account. This on-premises integration setting separates the two operations so users can unlock only.

questions.q: What is the status of SSPR with on-premises writeback when staged rollout is enabled for a security group?
options: It is fully supported for all users in the staged rollout group and requires no extra configuration
It isn't supported; it may work in some cases, but consistent behavior can't be guaranteed
It is supported only with pass-through authentication
It is supported only if Seamless SSO is also enabled
questions.explanation: Microsoft notes that SSPR with writeback isn't supported when staged rollout is enabled for a security group. Plan to finish the migration before relying on writeback for those users.

questions.q: What are the minimum and maximum password lengths in Microsoft Entra ID?
options: 6 and 128 characters
12 and 64 characters
10 and 127 characters
8 and 256 characters
questions.explanation: Entra ID passwords must be between 8 and 256 characters. For cloud-only users the minimum length can't be raised.

questions.q: Which statement about the Entra ID cloud password policy is correct?
options: Passwords require three of four character types, and the minimum length can't be raised for cloud-only users
Passwords require all four character types
The minimum length can be raised to 12 characters with an Entra ID P1 license and a custom policy
Passwords may contain Unicode characters
questions.explanation: Complexity requires three of four types (lowercase, uppercase, numbers, symbols). The 8-character minimum is fixed, and Unicode characters aren't allowed.

questions.q: A tenant created in 2024 has never configured password expiration. What is the default maximum password age?
options: 90 days, which applies to every tenant unless an administrator changes it
180 days
No expiration; passwords don't expire by default
30 days
questions.explanation: Tenants created after 2021 have no default expiration. Older tenants default to 90 days, and the value can be changed with Update-MgDomain.

questions.q: Which minimum role lets an administrator set particular cloud users' passwords to never expire with Microsoft Graph PowerShell?
options: Helpdesk Administrator
User Administrator
Security Reader
Authentication Policy Administrator
questions.explanation: Microsoft states that at least the User Administrator role can set user passwords not to expire using Graph PowerShell, by setting DisablePasswordExpiration on the user.

questions.q: What are the length constraints for a user principal name in Microsoft Entra ID?
options: A total of 113 characters, with up to 64 before the @ and up to 48 after it
A total of 256 characters, with up to 128 on each side of the @ symbol and no limit on the domain part
A total of 64 characters, with up to 32 on each side of the @
A total of 113 characters, with up to 48 before the @ and up to 64 after it
questions.explanation: A UPN can be up to 113 characters in total, with at most 64 characters before the @ symbol and 48 after it.

questions.q: Which character type is not allowed in Entra ID passwords?
options: Symbols such as @ and #
Blank spaces
Numbers
Unicode characters
questions.explanation: Allowed characters include letters, numbers, listed symbols and blank spaces, but Unicode characters aren't allowed.

questions.q: Which password protection capability applies to cloud-only users in every Entra ID edition, including Free?
options: The custom banned password list
Password protection for on-premises Active Directory
The global banned password list
Customizable smart lockout thresholds
questions.explanation: The Microsoft-maintained global banned password list is applied automatically to cloud accounts. The custom list, on-premises enforcement and smart lockout customization need P1 or higher.

questions.q: A company wants to ban its brand and product names in passwords. Which requirements apply?
options: Entra ID Free, Global Reader, and up to 100 terms
Entra ID P1 or higher, the Authentication Policy Administrator role, and a list of up to 1,000 terms
Entra ID P2 only, the Security Reader role, and up to 5,000 terms including regular expressions
Entra ID Governance, Authentication Administrator, and unlimited terms
questions.explanation: The custom banned password list requires P1 or higher and is limited to 1,000 terms. Configuration needs the Authentication Policy Administrator role, and the list is combined with the global list.

questions.q: How many points must a password score to be accepted by Entra Password Protection after normalization and matching?
options: Five
Three
Eight
Ten
questions.explanation: Each banned term earns one point and each remaining character earns one point, and the total must be at least five. For example, a short password built mostly from a banned term fails.

questions.q: Which statement about how Entra Password Protection matches banned terms is correct?
options: Only exact matches against the custom list are blocked, and the global list is used only for cloud sign-ins
Matching ignores the user's name and the tenant name
Passwords are normalized and fuzzy matched with an edit distance of one against the combined lists
Matching uses an edit distance of three
questions.explanation: The password is normalized (for example substituting look-alike characters), then fuzzy matched against global and custom terms with an edit distance of one. It also checks the user's first name, last name and tenant name.

questions.q: You deploy Entra Password Protection for on-premises Active Directory. How do the components communicate?
options: DC agents contact Entra ID directly over HTTPS and use the proxy service only for registration
The proxy service pushes policy to the DC agents
Entra Connect relays the policy to the DC agents
DC agents contact the proxy service, which contacts Entra ID; DC agents never call Entra ID directly
questions.explanation: The DC agent requests the policy from a proxy service over RPC, and the proxy downloads it from Entra ID. The proxy is stateless and never calls the DC agent.

questions.q: You are starting a deployment of on-premises Entra Password Protection. Which mode should you use first?
options: Enforced mode, because audit mode isn't supported on-premises and applies only to cloud accounts
Audit mode, which logs would-be rejections without blocking passwords
Enforced mode, but only for one domain
Disabled mode until every domain controller has an agent
questions.explanation: Microsoft recommends starting in audit mode, which evaluates passwords against the policy in a what-if mode, then switching to Enforced when you're comfortable with the impact.

questions.q: Enable password protection on Windows Server Active Directory is set to No. What do the deployed DC agents do?
options: They go quiescent: all passwords are accepted without validation and no audit events are generated
They keep validating passwords in audit mode and keep writing events to the event log
They enforce only the global banned list
They reject all password changes
questions.explanation: When the setting is No, DC agents stop validating and generate no audit events. Use Audit mode, not No, if you want to observe without blocking.

questions.q: A hybrid tenant with synced users wants the global banned password list enforced for on-premises Active Directory users. What is required?
options: Nothing; the global list applies to synced users with Entra ID Free once the sync tool is installed
Entra ID Governance
Only the DC agent, with no license
Entra ID P1 or P2, plus the proxy service and DC agent software
questions.explanation: For cloud-only users the global list is free. Protecting users synchronized from AD DS needs Entra ID P1 or P2, along with the DC agent and proxy deployment.

questions.q: When is a password evaluated against the banned password lists?
options: At every sign-in
Only when passwords expire
When a user changes or resets a password, not at sign-in
Only when a risk is detected
questions.explanation: Passwords are validated at change or reset events. Existing passwords aren't re-checked at sign-in, so banning a term doesn't invalidate current passwords.

questions.q: You install the DC agent on only two of five domain controllers and set the mode to Enforced. What is the effect?
options: The policy is enforced only for password changes processed by domain controllers that have the agent
The policy is enforced domain-wide because the agent syncs to all domain controllers
Enforcement fails until all domain controllers have the agent
The agent installs itself on the remaining domain controllers
questions.explanation: Incremental deployment is supported, but the password policy is enforced only where the DC agent is installed. Deploy to all DCs for consistent coverage.

questions.q: What are the default smart lockout settings in Azure public cloud tenants?
options: 5 failed attempts and a 30-second lockout
10 failed attempts and a 60-second lockout
3 failed attempts and a 60-second lockout
10 failed attempts and a 15-minute lockout
questions.explanation: By default, smart lockout locks the account for one minute after 10 failed attempts, and repeated lockouts increase the duration. Azure US Government tenants default to 3 attempts.

questions.q: What is required to customize the smart lockout threshold and duration?
options: Entra ID Free
Entra ID Governance
Entra ID P1 or higher
Entra ID P2 only
questions.explanation: Smart lockout is always on for everyone with default values, but customizing the settings requires Entra ID P1 or higher.

questions.q: How does smart lockout treat sign-in attempts from familiar and unfamiliar locations?
options: They share a single lockout counter
Attempts from familiar locations are never counted
Attempts from unfamiliar locations are blocked outright
They have separate lockout counters
questions.explanation: Smart lockout uses separate counters for familiar and unfamiliar locations so an attacker can lock out only the unfamiliar counter while the real user continues from familiar ones.

questions.q: A tenant uses pass-through authentication. How should you set the lockout values so Entra smart lockout protects on-premises accounts from being locked out?
options: Set the Entra threshold higher than the AD threshold and the Entra duration shorter than the AD duration
Set both Entra and AD to identical values
Set the Entra threshold lower than the AD threshold and the Entra lockout duration longer than the AD duration
Disable the AD lockout policy entirely
questions.explanation: Entra ID should lock first, so its threshold must be lower and its duration longer than the AD DS values. Remember Entra duration is in seconds and AD duration is in minutes.

questions.q: A user was locked out by smart lockout and doesn't want to wait for the lockout to expire. What can the user do?
options: Use SSPR and choose I forgot my password, which resets the lockout duration
Sign in from a new device
Wait for an administrator to disable smart lockout
Change their UPN suffix
questions.explanation: If the user chooses I forgot my password during SSPR, the lockout duration is reset to zero, so they don't need to wait. An SSPR reset can also reset the unfamiliar-location counter.

questions.q: Which smart lockout capability isn't available for tenants that use pass-through authentication?
options: Familiar location tracking
Tracking of the last bad password hash
Customizing the lockout threshold
Customizing the lockout duration
questions.explanation: Hash tracking isn't available with PTA because authentication happens on-premises, not in the cloud. Smart lockout thresholds and duration can still be set.

questions.q: Which feature gives federated AD FS deployments protection similar to smart lockout?
options: The Entra Password Protection DC agent
Seamless single sign-on
A Conditional Access sign-in frequency control
AD FS Extranet Smart Lockout
questions.explanation: AD FS 2016 and 2019 offer Extranet Lockout and Extranet Smart Lockout. Microsoft still recommends moving to managed authentication.
